meta.title: Processing Timelines for Foreign Investors — Saudi Arabia
meta.description: Estimated processing durations for key government procedures relevant to foreign investors establishing a business in Saudi Arabia. All durations are in business days unless otherwise noted. All entries are draft — durations have not been independently verified against live official sources or current processing benchmarks.
meta.last_verified: [PLACEHOLDER — update when entries are verified against current official processing benchmarks]

data.conditions: Processing begins after complete documentation is submitted. Simple cases may be approved within 1 business day. Regulated sectors requiring additional authority approvals take longer. Under the Investment Law (Royal Decree M/19, 2024), a single registration now covers multiple sectors. Source: MISA Investor Guide, 12th Edition, July 2025.
data.placeholder_reason: Verified per MISA Investor Guide, 12th Edition, July 2025. Min: 1 business day (straightforward cases). Max/typical: 10 business days. Regulated sectors requiring additional approvals may take longer.

data.conditions: Annual update of registration data as required by Investment Law Executive Regulations (Ministerial Decision 1086, February 2025). Must be completed within the period specified by MISA.
data.placeholder_reason: Verified per MISA Investor Guide, 12th Edition, July 2025.

data.conditions: Immediate (same day) for straightforward activities submitted with complete documentation via the Ministry of Commerce digital portal. Trade name review adds 1–2 business days for names requiring approval. Activities requiring sector regulator approval may take up to 7 business days or longer. Ejari electronic lease is mandatory — paper tenancy contracts are not accepted. Under the new CR Law (Royal Decree M/83, April 2025), a single national CR covers all activities and branches — no separate branch CR required or available. New CR numbers are 10 digits starting with '7'. Existing branch CRs: grace period until April 2030 to convert or cancel. Exception: foreign company branch CR remains valid if it is the sole KSA registered entity of that foreign company. Source: Ministry of Commerce service level benchmarks (2025).
data.placeholder_reason: Verified: immediate to 7 business days per Ministry of Commerce 2025 service benchmarks. Typical case (complete documentation, standard activity): 1 business day. Electronic lease (Ejari) is mandatory for the premises address. Verify current service levels at mc.gov.sa.

data.process_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening (Saudi Licensed Bank)
data.conditions: Processing time varies significantly by bank. Foreign-owned entities typically face additional due diligence requirements compared to Saudi-owned companies. Required documents typically include the CR, MISA investment registration certificate, and KYC documentation for all beneficial owners. Some banks have dedicated foreign investment onboarding teams.
data.placeholder_reason: Bank account opening timelines are not governed by a single authority — each SAMA-regulated bank sets its own processing standards. The authority_id is set to misa as the primary investor-facing authority, but the actual processing is by individual Saudi banks. Verify with the chosen bank and SAMA at sama.gov.sa.

placeholders.description: Bank account opening timelines vary by bank and entity type. No single official benchmark exists. Contact Saudi-licensed banks directly and review SAMA guidance at sama.gov.sa for applicable banking regulations.

Corporate banking is regulated by SAMA (sama.gov.sa) but processed by individual Saudi licensed banks. The same is not a single government body processing timeline. Verify with the specific bank and SAMA.

data.conditions: Work permits are issued to expatriate employees hired by a registered Saudi company. The employer must be in good Nitaqat standing. Processing includes MHRSD approval and coordination with the Absher platform. The employee must hold a valid visa category that permits the transition to a work permit.
data.placeholder_reason: The current work permit (tashreeh al-amal) processing time has not been independently verified. Processing times are affected by the employer's Nitaqat compliance status, the employee's nationality, and the specific activity. Verify at hrsd.gov.sa and via the Qiwa platform.

placeholders.description: The current MHRSD work permit processing time benchmark. Affected by Nitaqat status, employee nationality, and activity classification. Verify at hrsd.gov.sa.

data.conditions: An Iqama (residency permit) is issued to an expatriate employee after the work permit is approved, the employee has entered Saudi Arabia on the appropriate visa, and the employer registers the employee with the relevant authorities. The process involves MHRSD, the General Directorate of Passports (Jawazat), and the Absher platform.
data.placeholder_reason: Iqama processing times are not consistently published and vary by employee nationality, employer compliance status, and completeness of documentation. Verify current processing benchmarks with the relevant authorities and via the Absher Business platform.

placeholders.description: The current Iqama issuance processing time. Involves MHRSD and the General Directorate of Passports (Jawazat). Processing varies by nationality and employer status. Verify at hrsd.gov.sa and via the Absher Business platform.

Iqama issuance involves both MHRSD (labor clearance) and the General Directorate of Passports (Jawazat), which is under the Ministry of Interior. The primary entry point is via the Absher Business platform. authority_id is set to mhrsd as the primary employer-facing authority.

data.conditions: Application submitted online via MISA portal. Processing similar to standard investment registration. Mandatory RHQ activities must commence within 6 months of licensing. 3 optional activities required within 12 months. Minimum 15 full-time employees required by end of year 1, including at least 3 senior executives with prior experience at the group's global or regional headquarters. RHQ must be registered as an independent legal entity (LLC or branch). Cannot generate direct commercial revenue in Saudi Arabia — restricted to regional management, strategy, budgeting, and marketing functions.
data.placeholder_reason: Verified per setupinsaudi.com and Middle East Briefing (2025). Processing: 5–10 working days via MISA portal. Eligible for 0% CIT on qualifying RHQ activities (subject to conditions — verify at investsaudi.sa). Exempt from Saudization (Nitaqat) for RHQ-specific functions. Government contract eligibility requires active RHQ license (mandatory since January 2024).

data.conditions: Application submitted online via MISA portal after complete documentation is gathered. No established foreign parent company required. No minimum capital for most sectors (exception: SAR 25,000 for non-sole-proprietorships established outside KSA for over 1 year). 100% foreign ownership permitted. Requires support letter from a MISA-recognized incubator, accelerator, or VC firm. Business must be innovative, tech-enabled, or high-growth and aligned with Vision 2030 sectors (FinTech, HealthTech, AI, renewable energy, tourism, healthcare). Not available for standard IT services companies or traditional microbusinesses.
data.placeholder_reason: Verified per Wamda/Tawaref 2024, TASC 2025. Processing: 5–7 business days after complete documentation. Access to premium residency if startup raises SAR 400,000+ from authorized parties. Path to permanent residency if raises $4M and employs 10 staff for 1 year.

data.conditions: Employer submits registration via qiwa.sa after obtaining a valid Commercial Registration (CR). Registration is processed electronically. No fee. Activation is typically immediate or within 1 business day. Must be completed before hiring any employees.
data.placeholder_reason: Verified per qiwa.sa platform documentation (2025). Registration is immediate on the platform once CR is available. Typical processing: 1 business day for account activation. This step must precede any employment contract authentication or work permit application on the Qiwa platform.

data.conditions: Processing begins after the employee has entered Saudi Arabia on the correct visa and the employer submits the Iqama application via Muqeem. Required documents include: valid passport, entry visa, employment contract authenticated via Qiwa, GOSI registration, and medical examination clearance. Processing time varies by employee nationality, completeness of documentation, and Jawazat workload. Iqama must be issued within 90 days of the employee's arrival — late issuance triggers penalties.
data.placeholder_reason: Verified approximate range based on Muqeem/Jawazat published benchmarks and HRSD employer guidance (2025). Typical: 14–30 business days for standard cases. Complex or nationality-specific cases can reach 60 days. The 90-day statutory deadline from employee arrival is the hard deadline — employers should target Iqama issuance well before this limit. Verify current benchmarks at muqeem.sa.

data.conditions: Processing time after complete application submission. Eligibility: companies registered in prominent government programs, strategic companies (national or foreign), or companies not yet registered in the Kingdom. Fee payable within 30 days of classification approval notification.
data.placeholder_reason: Verified per MISA Investor Guide, 12th Edition, March 2025, Section 3.3.1 (misa.gov.sa/app/uploads/2025/03/Investor-Guide.pdf). Processing: 5 working days after complete application submission.

data.conditions: Timeline varies by bank and KYC complexity. Foreign-owned companies typically require additional due diligence compared to Saudi-owned entities. All prerequisites must be complete before the bank visit: active MISA IRC, valid CR, National Address, GM Iqama. Inactive accounts risk dormancy — maintain regular transactions after activation. Timeline is an estimate from practitioner experience; no single SAMA-published benchmark exists for foreign-entity onboarding. Verify with the chosen bank and SAMA at sama.gov.sa.
data.placeholder_reason: No single official SAMA-published benchmark for foreign-entity bank account opening. Estimated range of 7-28 business days based on multiple 2025-2026 practitioner sources. Verify with the chosen bank directly.

placeholders.description: Bank account opening timelines for foreign-owned companies are not published by a single authority. Each SAMA-regulated bank sets its own KYC and onboarding standards. The range of 7-28 days reflects practitioner experience across multiple banks and entity types in 2025-2026. Verify current processing benchmarks with your chosen bank and SAMA.
